name: GARRAFINA
description: Garrafina is a Spanish train domino game in which each player extends a personal train from a central starting double. Trains become open to opponents when their owner passes, creating a tactical open or private state on every branch.

content.text: Garrafina is a Spanish train domino game in which each player extends a personal train from a central starting double. Trains become open to opponents when their owner passes, creating a tactical open or private state on every branch.
Garrafina developed in Spanish domino circles as a trains-family game related to Mexican Train but with stricter ownership rules for each player's branch.
2 to 4 players; four-player is the base form.
One double-six domino set of 28 tiles.
Optional train markers to show which trains are open after a pass.
Deal 7 tiles to each player. In 4-player games all tiles are dealt. In 3-player games one 7-tile heap remains face down. In 2-player games two 7-tile heaps remain face down.

items.text: Three-Player Heap Exchange: With three players, one face-down 7-tile heap may be exchanged for a player's original hand under first-turn conditions; at most one exchange per deal.
Two-Player Double Heap: With two players there are two 7-tile heaps; exchange may happen twice. If the loser exchanged twice, loss can be multiplied accordingly.
Correlativa: Mexican variant without full-hand exchange. Unplayed tiles stay in boneyard; blocked players draw one by one until playable or boneyard empty.
